answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a challenge-bound chain of sequential modular squarings, with each result needed to compute the next. A clone cannot skip steps or accelerate its own chain by distributing it across GPUs; it must incur the delay. Separate clones can run in parallel, so the bottleneck is per identity, not global. The dawn-to-dusk wait, not a whisper of extra hardware, sets the ledge an attacker must cross.
